overview: White has taken on e5 and Black plays 2...Nc6 as a gambit, wanting ...g5 and ...g4 or quick piece play against the f-file. White keeps the pawn with 3.Nf3 and returns it when necessary, with a big lead in material. Black's counterplay is thin, and the line is rare.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the extra e5 pawn with Nf3 and d4 and develop safely
Return the pawn to deal with the attack on the kingside
Use the half-open f-file against Black's kingside

black_ideas.idea: Play ...g5 and ...g4 with a pawn storm
Win the e5 pawn back with ...Nxe5 or ...Qe7

typical_structures.structure: White extra pawn on e5 with Black attacking it
Open f-file and a pawn storm on the kingside

character.notes: A gambit with an exposed white king; one slip loses fast for either side.

gambit.notes: White can keep the e5 pawn; Black has only development for it.

soundness.notes: Black's counterplay is thin, so it is dubious (low confidence).

structure.notes: Open e- and f-files, no pawn centre; open.

approach.notes: A rare gambit; strong players seldom play it.

level.notes: A dubious line is not for beginners.

character.reason: A gambit with open lines and mutual risk.

gambit.reason: Black has given the e-pawn and White can hold it.

soundness.reason: Black gets little for the pawn.

structure.reason: The e5 pawn and the f-file are open.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner.

plans.reason: Black develops fast and storms with ...g5.
